brief.ask: Set the art direction for 16 sports evites by sport type (basketball, football, soccer, baseball, hockey, motor racing, tennis, volleyball, golf, swimming, gymnastics, boxing, skate, cheer, track, martial arts) for birthdays, team parties and watch parties.
constraints: Surface: Plajah Evites, an invitation opened on a phone browser by guests who never sign up; also shared as a link preview and QR.

Build method (fixed): each design is a layered Tela document: a generated art plate, separate transparent foreground cut-outs that drift and react to phone tilt, a WebGL effects layer (foil shimmer, light leaks, bokeh, particles, candle flicker) revealed through masks, and live text in Tela. Names, dates and venues are never baked into the art.
Bar: consumer-facing, jaw-dropping, high-end professional. Must stay legible at 390px wide, honour reduced motion, and load fast on mobile data.
No copyrighted characters; kids art is original or Plajah-owned.

Production is GENERATIVE ONLY (Magnific image models, shaders, procedural code, renders of Plajah-owned 3D assets). One Magnific draft grid returns 8 to 16 distinct plates for a flat cost, so a whole collection can be explored in one or two prompts: direct those prompts.
No leagues, teams, logos, jerseys with numbers, or real athletes.
references: Exploration grid: 16 cinematic arena still-lifes, one per sport, dramatic stadium lighting, calm lower third. Strong and consistent.

proposals.title: The Measure of the Game
proposals.idea: Each evite is a single governed light source — a motivated stadium beam — that organises the art plate, the foil layer, the foreground drift, and the type hierarchy into one spatial argument, so that opening the card is not decoration but descent into the arena.
proposals.geometry: Portrait 390×844px canvas divided by a strict 12-column, 8-row modular grid with a 16px base unit. A single golden-section horizon line sits at row 5 — the floor of the arena — and every element anchors to it or hangs from it: the sport object occupies the upper field (rows 1–5) in a centred axis; the calm lower third (rows 6–8) is reserved for live text, held in a 10-column measure with 1-column gutters. No element crosses the horizon without earning it structurally. The 16 plates share this skeleton exactly; what changes is the spatial drama within each upper field.
proposals.typography: Heading: Playfair Display (OFL) — condensed capitals, tracking +80, size 28px at 390px — used only for sport name and party type in the lower third. Body / date / venue: Source Sans 3 (OFL), Regular, 14px, case-sensitive, tracking +20. A hairline rule (1px, 40% white) separates heading from body. No decorative type in the art plate; all live text sits in the Tela text layer above the WebGL mask. The scale ratio between heading and body is exactly 2:1 — a classical diapason — so the hierarchy reads as interval, not accident.
proposals.imageLogic: One Magnific draft-grid prompt returns all 16 plates in a single pass: '16 cinematic arena still-lifes, one per sport — basketball, football, soccer, baseball, hockey, motor racing, tennis, volleyball, golf, swimming, gymnastics, boxing, skateboarding, cheer, track, martial arts — each a single dramatic overhead-angled stadium key light striking the central sport object against a deep shadow field, photorealistic material detail, no people, no logos, no numbers, no league marks, calm lower third in soft ambient fill, consistent horizon line at 60 percent of frame height, consistent square crop, 8-bit cinematic colour grade, film grain, lens vignette.' The plates are editorial selections from that grid — not retouched, not composited with external photography. The motivated light source coordinates are extracted per plate and fed as a uniform vec2 into the WebGL foil shader, so shimmer di
proposals.texture: Simulated paper tooth from a procedural normal-map shader (Perlin noise, 0.4 amplitude, 120px grain scale) applied as a multiply-blend overlay at 18% opacity — present in both the art plate render directive and the WebGL layer, so the substrate reads as continuous. Foil is a WebGL anisotropic-highlight shader locked to the plate's light-source vector; it activates only on the sport object silhouette mask, not the full frame. No decorative texture added to the lower third — it reads clean against the grained upper field, which creates a natural figure-ground separation without a rule or a box.
proposals.motion: Sequence is governed like a three-voice canon: (1) On load, 0–400ms: the art plate fades from black via an iris-reveal centred on the motivated light source — not a generic dissolve but a radial unmask that traces the beam. (2) 400–900ms: foreground cut-out (the sport object as a separate transparent layer) settles 6px downward on a spring-physics arc — damping ratio 0.7, stiffness 180 — arriving at rest exactly at the golden-section horizon. (3) 900ms onward: WebGL foil shimmer activates as a slow breathing oscillation (0.3Hz sinusoid) tied to phone tilt via deviceorientation API; if tilt unavailable or reduced-motion preferred, shimmer holds at a static highlight position derived from the light-source vec2. Type fades in at 900ms, 200ms duration, no transform — it does not animate, it arrives. Total motion budget: under 1.2 seconds to full legibility.
proposals.productionMethod: Step 1: One Magnific prompt (as specified in imageLogic) returns 16 plates as a single grid image; editorial selection identifies the strongest 16 crops. Step 2: Magnific upscale pass on each selected plate to 1170×2532px (3x retina) with film-grain and lens-vignette directives preserved. Step 3: For each plate, a secondary Magnific inpainting pass isolates the sport object as a clean-edge transparent PNG foreground cut-out (prompt: 'extract [sport object] on transparent background, match existing lighting, no shadow on alpha'). Step 4: WebGL shader (GLSL, Plajah-owned codebase) receives per-plate light-source vec2 as a uniform; foil and paper-tooth overlays are procedural, no additional asset cost. Step 5: Tela document assembly — art plate as background layer, foreground PNG as drift layer, WebGL mask layer, live text layer on top. Names, dates, venues are never baked. Step 6: Link-pre
proposals.humanTrace: The governing light source is an editorial decision made once per plate by a director who reads the beam — its angle, its falloff, its relationship to the object — and records it as a coordinate pair that then governs every downstream system. That act of reading and naming a light is the human trace: not a brushstroke, but a judgment that propagates through shader, motion arc, and type placement, the way a conductor's tempo decision propagates through every instrument's phrase length.
proposals.risk: The strict modular grid and the shared horizon line make all 16 cards feel like a coherent series — which is the goal — but it also risks making them feel like a product system rather than individual celebrations. A birthday card for a seven-year-old gymnast and a watch-party card for adult hockey fans must both feel personal. The risk is worth carrying because the grid is a skeleton, not a surface: the art plate's dramatic variation — a beam catching a balance beam in chalk dust versus a puck on ice versus a boxing glove in shadow — provides all the emotional differentiation needed, and the structural consistency is what gives the collection the professional weight the brief demands. If the grid becomes a cage, the image must break it; but I will not break it arbitrarily.

I am proposing an iris-reveal that traces the motivated beam quietly and stops. The Dramatist will call this restraint timid; I call their flourish an announcement that competes with the content. proposals.title: Proof of Contact
proposals.idea: Each evite is a found artifact from the game itself — a surface that was struck, scraped, dragged, or pressured by the sport — so the invitation carries forensic evidence of play rather than a celebration of it.
proposals.geometry: Portrait 9:16 phone crop. No centered medallion. The plate is divided by a single diagonal fault line — not decorative, physically motivated by the sport's dominant force vector (puck trajectory, punch angle, launch angle off a golf tee). Lower third is a crushed, low-contrast zone — ink-dense, matte — where live text sits without competing. Upper two-thirds is the arena artifact. No symmetry. No safe frame.
proposals.typography: Familjen Grotesk (OFL, Google Fonts) for event name: heavy weight, condensed tracking, all caps, set at an angle that mirrors the fault line within ±5°. Instrument Serif (OFL) for supporting details — date, venue — in small, upright, tracked-loose italic. No decorative headline face. The type is a label on evidence, not a poster headline. Minimum 18px body for 390px legibility. Contrast ratio ≥ 4.5:1 against the crushed lower third at all times.
proposals.imageLogic: Magnific generative still-lifes directed as 16-cell grid: each plate is the sport's primary contact surface photographed in raking forensic light — basketball leather pore-deep with court dust ground in, hockey ice with a blade-cut groove catching a single sodium source from above, boxing canvas with a resin-darkened impact shadow, golf green with a spike-mark cluster, swim-lane water surface at the exact moment a hand entry breaks it — all shot as if by a crime-scene photographer who loves the game. No athletes. No equipment as hero prop. The surface IS the subject. Raking light from one motivated source per plate, physically plausible, never centered. Foreground cut-out layer: one loose, generative debris element per sport (chalk dust cloud, water bead cluster, loose tape curl, grass divot clod) rendered with alpha edges that are deliberately ragged — not clean masks.
proposals.texture: Simulated coarse-grain silver gelatin print tooth — paper fiber visible at 100% zoom, generated via Magnific texture overlay pass. Ink-bleed halftone vignette in the lower third, not as decoration but as a logical consequence of the dense ink zone. The WebGL foil layer is locked exclusively to the fault-line edge and the debris cut-out perimeter: it proves those edges are physically uneven because smooth foil over a smooth edge reads as decoration, but foil clinging to a ragged chalk-dust outline reads as varnish over a real event. No foil in the lower text zone. Reduced-motion fallback: foil layer drops entirely, fault line holds, everything still reads.
proposals.motion: Phone loads: plate arrives first, static, 0.3s. Fault line pulses once — a single pressure wave traveling its length at 0.6s, as if the impact just happened — then holds. Debris cut-out drifts on gyroscope tilt: slow parallax, 2–4px travel max, eased. Foil shimmer along fault edge and debris perimeter responds to tilt simultaneously. Candle/bokeh particles rise slowly in upper field — 8 max, low opacity, 0.4s stagger — representing arena light flare, not celebration. No looping animation. No autoplay sound. Total motion budget: under 2.5s to settled state. Reduced motion: no drift, no particles, foil static, fault line static. All information present from frame zero.
proposals.productionMethod: Magnific prompt grid, two passes: Pass 1 — 16-cell forensic still-life grid, one sport per cell, raking single-source light, no humans, no branding, ultra-detail surface texture, silver-gelatin film simulation, 9:16 crop with calm lower third. Pass 2 — 16-cell debris element grid, sport-matched, transparent-ready alpha subjects, same lighting direction as Pass 1 plate. WebGL shader written procedurally: fault-line geometry is parameterized by sport (angle input), foil mask is generated from edge-detection of the debris alpha. Tela document structure: generated plate (bottom), debris cut-out (middle, tilt-reactive), WebGL effects (top, masked to fault edge + debris perimeter), live text layer (always on top, never baked). All 16 share one shader, one Tela template — only the plate, debris asset, fault angle, and sport-accent hue vary.
proposals.humanTrace: The forensic raking light is a single committed direction per plate — it is a record of a decision about where the source is, and every surface detail is subordinate to that decision. The fault-line angle is derived from sport physics, not aesthetic preference: it can be argued about and changed, which means it was chosen. The debris alpha edges are ragged by directive — the Magnific prompt specifies uneven, fibrous, physically-plausible edges, not clean cutouts. The foil proving the wood-was-carved rule: it clings only to the uneven, not to the resolved.
proposals.risk: The plates look like forensic documents, not party invitations — some clients will read them as cold or institutional. The risk is worth it because game-day electricity is not confetti; it is the residue of contact, and if the surface carries that residue the guest feels the game before they read the date. A plate this specific also survives being shared as a link preview thumbnail at 200px — the fault line and raking light read at thumbnail scale in a way that a busy illustrated arena scene does not. The risk is legibility of tone, not legibility of text.

arguesWith.why: The Baroque Dramatist will load the upper field with volumetric god-rays, smoke, and multiple competing light sources to manufacture electricity. I am against this because drama manufactured from multiple sources proves nothing happened — it is a simulation of consequence without the cause. One raking source that makes the ice groove cast a shadow two millimeters long is more electric than a stadi

proposals.title: State Variables, Game Conditions
proposals.idea: Each evite is a physically-simulated arena instrument — one declared light source, three depth planes, and a single sport-specific physics rule — so every shimmer angle, parallax gain, and particle behavior is a derivable consequence of that declaration, not a decorative choice.
proposals.geometry: Portrait 9:16, 390px wide. Three declared depth planes: background plate (arena environment, full bleed), mid-plane (sport object — ball, puck, racket, chalk cloud — floating as transparent cut-out, 1.8× parallax gain), foreground plane (type zone, lower 28% of canvas, 0.4× parallax gain, highest z). Grid logic: the sport object always occupies the optical center ±12px — not randomly placed — because it is the input that changes per sport and must read identically in link-preview crop (1200×630 letterboxed). Lower third is a ruled band: 2px top stroke, semi-transparent dark field, live text only. No baked names, dates, or venues anywhere in the art plate.
proposals.typography: Space Grotesk (Google Fonts / OFL) for all display and body — its geometric skeleton reads as engineered, its ink-trap corners give it warmth without nostalgia. Weights: 700 for event type label (all-caps, 0.18em tracking), 400 for date/venue (sentence case, tight). Secondary: Space Mono for any numeric field (time, score-style countdown if implemented) — monospace prevents layout shift as digits update. No decorative script. No serif. Case rule: sport label is capslock; host name is title case; all else sentence case. Minimum 16px rendered size on 390px canvas.
proposals.imageLogic: Magnific generative grid prompt directed as follows — Prompt A (8 plates, sports 1–8: basketball, football, soccer, baseball, hockey, motor racing, tennis, volleyball): '8-panel cinematic arena still-life grid, one sport per panel, dramatic single-source stadium key light from upper-left at 35 degrees, photorealistic sport object centered at optical midpoint, deep bokeh background with arena seats out of focus, no people, no logos, no jersey numbers, no text, neutral lower third in shadow, aspect ratio 9:16, each panel a distinct sport, consistent light direction and color temperature 5600K across all panels, film-grain overlay, shallow depth of field, hyper-detailed object surface.' Prompt B (8 plates, sports 9–16: golf, swimming, gymnastics, boxing, skate, cheer, track, martial arts): identical framing instruction, new sport objects. The 16 plates return as one flat-cost grid. Editoria
proposals.texture: Simulated physical surface, not applied filter. Background plate carries stadium concrete and seat-fabric texture generated into the image. Mid-plane object carries material-accurate surface: leather seam on basketball, ice-scratch refraction on puck, chalk dust particle field on gymnastics grip — all generated. WebGL foil shimmer is angle-locked to the declared light source (upper-left 35°): highlight rotates only within a ±22° arc as phone tilts, never omnidirectional, because the light source is a constraint not an aesthetic. Bokeh falloff origin is pinned to the same declared source. Scratch-reveal mask on lower-third band exposes a secondary color field underneath — the scratch direction is derived from the light angle (shadow falls lower-right, scratches run upper-left to lower-right). Film grain: 12% opacity luminance noise, static not animated, preserves perceived film weight wit
proposals.motion: Declared physics rule per sport — this is the system, not decoration. Rule structure: [object type] → [physics constant] → [tilt response]. Basketball: gyroscopic spin arc, object rotates 8° per 15° phone tilt on y-axis, 12fps stepped (not eased) to read as physical, not floating. Football: wobble oscillation, ±4° tumble on x-axis, 8fps. Soccer: pendulum swing, 6° arc, 10fps. Baseball: slow rotation, 5° per tilt, continuous. Hockey puck: lateral slide, translates 6px per 10° tilt, no rotation. Motor racing: none — helmet static, particle stream (spark trail) extends 12px on tilt. Tennis: bounce simulation, object drops 8px and returns on tap event. Volleyball: float drift, 4px translation, 16fps smooth. Golf: none — ball static, grass-blade particle field sways 3px on tilt. Swimming: water-surface refraction ripple, not object movement. Gymnastics: chalk-dust particle burst on load, sett
proposals.productionMethod: Two Magnific prompt runs return 16 background plates and 16 isolated foreground objects (transparent PNG, second pass). Plates imported into Tela as locked art layer. Cut-outs placed on mid-plane layer with Tela's tilt-parallax binding — parallax gain set per sport per the physics rule above. WebGL effects layer (foil, bokeh, particles) built as a single reusable shader module parameterized by: light_angle (fixed at 315°), sport_id (integer 1–16, controls particle type and physics constant), plane_count (3, fixed). Lower-third live text zone is a Tela text block — zero baked content. QR and link-preview crop are auto-generated from the 1200×630 letterbox of the same composition. No commissioned art, no photo shoot, no physical build. The entire collection is one Tela template with 16 sport-parameter states.
proposals.humanTrace: Editorial selection of which plate to use per sport — the human judgment is which generated image places the object at the correct optical center with the deepest lower-third shadow. The physics constants per sport (spin rate, tilt gain, particle count) are authored decisions, not defaults. Foil arc limit (±22°) is a constraint I am writing as a system rule, not a setting someone toggled. The scratch direction on the lower-third mask is derived by hand from the light angle — it is calculated, not random. These are the perceptible signs of making: a system someone thought through, not a template someone filled in.
proposals.risk: The physics-rule-per-sport system is invisible to most guests — they feel it but cannot name it. The risk is that the coherence reads as coldness, that the instrument feels like a dashboard rather than a party invitation. That risk is worth it because the alternative — 16 decorative treatments with glow effects and no underlying rule — produces work that is indistinguishable from every other sports evite template on the market. The system is what makes this collection a collection rather than a folder of images. And the physics constants can be tuned toward warmth without abandoning the architecture.

arguesWith.why: The Baroque Dramatist will want a reveal moment — a cinematic wipe, a dramatic zoom, a light-leak crescendo on open. I expect the argument that without a theatrical entrance sequence, the evite fails to produce the jaw-drop the brief demands. My counter: a reveal is a one-time event; a behavior is something the guest discovers for thirty seconds while tilting their phone and then shows someone els

proposals.title: Field Notes, Game Night
proposals.idea: Each evite is a documentary field-notebook plate — a generative arena still-life treated as if a working photographer's loupe and a cartographer's registration mark landed on the same spread — so the sport's physical world (the court grain, the ice rut, the chalk line, the mat weave) becomes the invitation's primary argument, not decoration.
proposals.geometry: Portrait 9:16 card, 390px wide. A ruled field-notebook grid underlies every plate — not decorative lines but a faint 8-column, 14-row cartographic mesh, slightly off-true by 1.5° to suggest a hand-laid sheet. The art plate occupies the upper 62% (golden-ratio cut). A calm lower third — the 38% — holds live text on a material ground that differs per sport: compressed cork (tennis), rubberized track surface (track), waxed linen (boxing). The foreground cut-out layer floats one hero object per sport — the ball, the puck, the skate, the ribbon — centered above the text seam, drifting 6px on tilt.
proposals.typography: Headlines: Libre Baskerville Bold, 28–32px, tracked +20, sentence case — an expedition logbook register, not a scoreboard shout. Event details: Source Sans 3 Regular, 14px, tracked +10, all-caps. Sport label (e.g. 'BASKETBALL / BIRTHDAY'): Libre Baskerville Italic, 11px, tracked +80, set flush-left in the lower third, functioning as a caption. No display typeface borrowed from any league identity. Second-script readiness: Source Sans 3 carries Latin, Cyrillic, Greek; Libre Baskerville covers Latin and Cyrillic. For any community where a second script is primary, the live-text layer swaps face to Noto Serif or Noto Sans — both OFL — without art-plate rebuild.
proposals.imageLogic: One Magnific prompt generates a 4×4 draft grid: 16 cinematic arena still-lifes, each a single sport, dramatic motivated stadium light raking from upper-left at 22°, hero equipment in sharp foreground, mid-ground depth blur, calm lower-third negative space. Prompt directive: 'No uniforms with numbers, no logos, no identifiable athlete faces; photograph-feel but generative; each plate a different sport surface — parquet, ice, clay, turf, pool tile, gymnastics floor, ring canvas, concrete skate surface, fairway grass, velodrome, sand court, boxing ring felt, track rubber, mat, balance beam chalk, motor-racing tarmac; stadium practise-light atmosphere, not match-day floodlights; lower 38% intentionally underexposed for live text legibility.' Editorial pass selects 16 finals from the grid. No retouching budget — Magnific's own upscale pass is the finish layer. The motivated 22° light angle is
proposals.texture: The art plate carries simulated film grain (procedural, 0.18 opacity, luminance-only) matching a pushed ISO-800 documentary film stock — not a filter, a WebGL grain shader seeded per-card so grain is unique per invite. The lower-third material ground is sport-specific: for basketball, compressed hardwood-end-grain generated from a Plajah-owned 3D cylinder render; for swimming, a frosted pool-tile render; for martial arts, woven jute mat generated procedurally. The cartographic mesh is printed as a 0.4px rule in a warm off-white, set at 8% opacity — visible on close inspection, invisible at a glance. No motif is borrowed from any living cultural community without a named collaboration gate; the only 'cultural' material is sport-surface vernacular, which is equipment, not heritage.
proposals.motion: Entrance (0–0.4s): the art plate fades up from black, grain resolves last, as if a darkroom print appearing. Hero object (0.4–0.8s): the foreground cut-out drops in from 12px above its rest position with a 0.4s ease-out — one gesture, no bounce. Foil shimmer: idle, breathing at 0.08Hz on the lower-third material ground only — not the art plate, not the typography. Tilt parallax: foreground cut-out drifts ±6px on device gyroscope, art plate drifts ±2px in the opposite direction, text layer is fixed. Candle-flicker WebGL: not used here — this is stadium practise light, steady, not ceremony. Bokeh particles: 4–6 slow-drifting light-leak orbs in the upper-right quadrant of the art plate only, 0.03Hz, referencing arena practise-light sodium haze. Reduced-motion: all motion collapses to a single 0.3s crossfade; grain is static; parallax off; foil shimmer off. Nothing is ever lost editorially —
proposals.productionMethod: One Magnific 4×4 prompt call returns 16 art plates. Prompt is written to lock the 22° light angle, underexposed lower third, and sport-surface specificity across all 16 in one generation pass. A second Magnific call, if needed, generates 8–16 foreground cut-out objects (ball, puck, skate, etc.) on neutral-grey ground for clean masking by Tela's generative-cutout pipeline. All 3D material grounds for the lower third are rendered from Plajah-owned primitive geometry (cylinder end-grain, tile grid, woven mesh) via a Blender/EEVEE headless render or equivalent procedural shader — no scan, no photograph. WebGL grain and foil shimmer are a single shared GLSL fragment shader with per-card seed and the 22° angle as a passed uniform. Tela live-text layer is templated once and inherits sport label, event type, and second-script font swap from the card data model. Total generative cost: two Magnifi
proposals.humanTrace: The 22° motivated light angle is the editorial decision that runs all the way through — it is chosen by a human, locked in the Magnific prompt, enforced as a WebGL shader uniform, and echoed in the parallax shadow offset. That single angle is the provenance chain. The grain shader is seeded per-card, so no two invites are identical — the 'photographer's hand' survives as statistical variation. The cartographic mesh offset of 1.5° is a fixed editorial choice, not an algorithm default. The sport-surface lower-third material is selected per sport by a human art director matching surface to sport vernacular. These are the perceptible signs of making: a chosen angle of light, a chosen degree of drift, a chosen surface underfoot.
proposals.risk: The documentary register — field notebook, practise light, cork and canvas — risks reading as quiet in a genre that expects noise. A parent opening a birthday invite may want confetti, not a photographer's loupe. The counter-argument is that jaw-dropping at consumer scale is now achieved by restraint and specificity, not by shouting; the grain and the foil shimmer and the drifting ball do the electricity work that a neon gradient used to. The deeper risk is that 'documentary' can tip into generic editorial minimalism — the very flattening I argue against. The guard against that is the sport-surface lower third: hardwood end-grain is not the same as pool tile is not the same as jute mat, and that specificity is what keeps each card from being a palette swap of the others.

arguesWith.why: The Baroque Dramatist will reach for gold leaf across all 16 plates and call it grandeur — but gold applied uniformly to basketball and gymnastics and motor racing alike is not grandeur, it is wallpaper. My foil shimmer is gated to the lower-third material ground only, at 0.08Hz, because it is earned by the specific surface it sits on. The Dramatist borrows gold before asking whose gold and what s

proposals.title: The Arena Breathes Before Kickoff
proposals.idea: Each evite is a miniature opera house: a single generative cinematic still-life — sport equipment and arena atmosphere caught in the suspended second before the opening whistle — lit by one motivated dramatic source that propagates its angle into foil shimmer, shadow depth, and bokeh origin simultaneously, so the invitation itself feels like standing in the tunnel mouth about to walk into the roar.
proposals.geometry: Portrait 9:16 card, 390px wide. The plate occupies the full bleed top 72% — no safe margins, edge-to-edge drama. A stepped lower third drops in three distinct horizontal registers: a razor-thin rule (2px, foil-shimmer WebGL mask), then a mid-register event-type lockup in oversized condensed caps, then a compact live-text zone for name/date/venue. The lower third is never more than 28% of the card height, keeping the arena plate sovereign. On link preview (1200×630 OG), the plate crops to its cinematic center and the rule + sport lockup survive the crop. QR sits bottom-right of the lower third, sized to tap-target minimum, never overlapping the art.
proposals.typography: Primary display: Barlow Condensed ExtraBold (Google Fonts / OFL) — all caps, tracked +80, sized between 48–64px for the sport/event-type lockup. Secondary live text (name, date, venue): Barlow Regular, 14–16px, tracked +20, sentence case. The condensed weight gives vertical breathing room so the plate is never crowded. No script faces; the drama comes from the image, not decorative letterforms. Reduced-motion fallback collapses the lockup to static with no animation but preserves weight and scale.
proposals.imageLogic: One Magnific draft-grid prompt returns all 16 plates in a single pass. Prompt direction: '16 cinematic arena still-life photographs, one per sport — basketball, football, soccer, baseball, hockey, motor racing, tennis, volleyball, golf, swimming, gymnastics, boxing, skateboarding, cheer, track, martial arts — each plate a dramatic stadium or venue environment lit by a single high-contrast motivated source (rim light from above-left at 30°), sport-specific equipment and atmosphere filling the frame, no people, no logos, no jersey numbers, no team colours, calm empty lower-third with natural vignette, film grain 35mm, aspect ratio 9:16, photorealistic, jaw-dropping, consistent lighting grammar across all 16 frames.' The 30° above-left source is the spatial constant that makes the collection read as a unified set — every shadow falls the same direction, every foil shimmer in the WebGL layer
proposals.texture: Simulated 35mm film grain at 18% opacity over the full plate — not a filter, a procedural shader layer that responds to brightness so grain is densest in the midtones, near-absent in the specular highlights (leaving foil shimmer clean). The razor rule uses the existing Tela WebGL foil-shimmer mask: gold-to-white gradient, animated at 0.4s ease-in-out on card open, reduced to a static gold line under prefers-reduced-motion. The lower third has a micro-texture of pressed paper tooth (procedural noise, 4px scale, 8% opacity) so the text zone feels physically distinct from the arena plate above — a stage apron versus the stage itself.
proposals.motion: Sequence: (1) Card opens — plate fades in over 0.6s, no movement yet. (2) At 0.6s the foil rule draws left-to-right over 0.4s, catching the light. (3) At 0.9s the sport/event-type lockup rises 8px into position over 0.3s, easing out — not a bounce, a landing. (4) Live text (name, date, venue) fades in at 1.1s over 0.2s. (5) After 1.5s, the foreground cut-out layer activates: sport-specific floating objects (a basketball, a starting block, a boxing glove, sport-matched per card) drift very slowly — parallax on phone tilt, maximum 6px displacement, 60fps. (6) WebGL bokeh particles pulse at 0.8Hz in the upper atmosphere of the plate, originating from the motivated light source position. All motion is interruptible. Reduced-motion: only steps 1 and 4 execute — plate fades in, text fades in, nothing else moves.
proposals.productionMethod: Single Magnific batch prompt (16-up grid, one flat cost) generates the arena plates. Plates are imported into Tela as the locked bottom art layer. Sport-specific foreground cut-out objects (ball, equipment silhouette) are generated as separate Magnific passes with transparent-background prompts, then placed on the drift layer in Tela. The WebGL effects layer (foil shimmer on rule, bokeh particles, film grain shader) is written once as a shared Tela component and parameterised by light-source XY position baked from the plate — so each of the 16 cards gets correctly positioned bokeh without manual adjustment. Lower-third live-text zone is a Tela template slot: name, date, venue, QR are never rasterised. Total generative passes: 2 Magnific grids (plates + cut-outs) + 1 shared shader component.
proposals.humanTrace: Editorial direction of the Magnific prompt: the choice to lock the motivated light source at 30° above-left across all 16 frames is a human compositional decision, not a model default. The stepped lower-third register heights (72/2px/10/16%) are measured decisions about where the eye rests before it reads. The 0.4s foil rule draw — timed to feel like a curtain rising rather than a loading artifact — is a performance decision. The grain shader's behaviour (densest in midtones, absent in specular) is a physically-plausible simulation of film stock, directed not generated.
proposals.risk: The risk is that 16 cards sharing identical lighting grammar read as one card with a sport swap — the collection cohesion becomes sameness. The counter is that the sport-specific equipment, venue atmosphere, and foreground cut-out objects do the differentiating work that the light intentionally does not; the light is the architecture, the objects are the performance. A second risk: the lower-third paper-tooth texture reads as muddy on low-brightness OLED screens at small sizes. Mitigation: the procedural noise is brightness-clamped so it never darkens the text zone below WCAG AA contrast on any background the plate produces. The risk is worth it because the alternative — 16 cards with 16 different lighting grammars — is a catalogue, not a collection, and a catalogue has no game-day electricity.

arguesWith.why: The Radical Minimalist will argue that the lower third should be a single line of text on white with maximum air, and that the foil rule is decorative noise. I argue back: the foil rule is not decoration, it is a threshold — the physical seam between the arena and the invitation, the moment the curtain parts. Removing it does not create clarity; it removes the only moment of tactile transition bet

proposals.title: One Thing. Pure Signal.
proposals.idea: Each evite is a single sport object held in extreme negative space — the object is the only decoration, the silence around it is the invitation.
proposals.geometry: 390px fixed column, no bleed. A centered vertical axis. The art plate occupies a 1:1 square cropped from the exact horizontal center of the screen — object fills no more than 38% of that square, surrounded by structured void. Below the square: a single hairline rule at 1px, then a calm lower-third live-text zone at fixed 96px height. No bleeds, no full-bleed drama. The hairline is load-bearing.
proposals.typography: Space Grotesk (OFL) — one weight only: Medium 500. Sport title in 11px all-caps tracked at 0.35em, centered above the hairline. Party name and date in 22px sentence-case below. No bold, no italic, no hierarchy beyond scale differential. The silence in the letterforms matches the silence in the plate.
proposals.imageLogic: Magnific prompt directed as one 4×4 grid call: '16 sport objects — basketball, football, soccer ball, baseball, hockey puck, racing helmet, tennis ball, volleyball, golf ball, swim goggle, gymnastics ribbon, boxing glove, skateboard deck, cheerleader megaphone, starting block, martial arts belt — each isolated on near-black or near-white ground, single raking sidelight from hard source at 15 degrees, no shadow fill, no environment, no human presence, photorealistic material rendering, 390×390px, 16 distinct plates.' Editorial selection keeps only the plate where the object's shadow is the second subject. Every other plate is discarded.
proposals.texture: The generated object surface carries physically-plausible material: leather seam catch, rubber matte, chrome visor reflection, silk ribbon sheen — all simulated by Magnific's material pass. No added grain, no overlay. The texture lives only in the object. The void is clean.
proposals.motion: Gyroscope tilt shifts the object layer 4px on x-axis and 3px on y-axis at 60fps — the shadow moves with it, which is the only proof of depth. The void does not move. On reduced-motion: object is static, shadow is static, the hairline pulses once at 0.3s opacity 0.4 to 1.0 and stops. Nothing else animates. The WebGL foil shimmer is applied only to the object's specular highlight pass — a 2px zone of iridescence that travels with tilt. No particles, no bokeh, no candle flicker on this direction.
proposals.productionMethod: Single Magnific 4×4 grid prompt returns 16 candidate plates at flat cost. Each selected plate is composited in Tela as: (1) base plate — near-black or near-white void with object, (2) object silhouette cut-out on transparent layer for tilt parallax, (3) WebGL foil shader bound to specular mask — 2px highlight band only, (4) live-text zone below hairline in Tela's text layer. Shadow is baked into plate — it does not parallax, which creates the depth illusion. QR and link-preview crop to the 1:1 square; the object reads at thumbnail scale because it is the only thing there.
proposals.humanTrace: The raking 15-degree hard light on each object is a directorial choice — the angle, the shadow length, the refusal of fill — and that choice is the human mark. Magnific executes; the decision about which shadow length makes the void articulate is editorial, not algorithmic.
proposals.risk: At 390px, a 38%-fill object in a void risks reading as unfinished or sparse to an audience expecting game-day maximalism. That risk is worth it because the silence is exactly the contrast that carries the meaning — every other direction in the room will be loud; this one will be the one guests pause on before tapping.

I disagree: electricity is contrast, not volume. A single basketball under a hard sidelight in 90% void contains more tension than a collage of ten elements fighting for attention. disputes.objection: A system that declares its own physics constants as the governing logic — spin rate, tilt gain, particle count varied per sport — is not a unified grammar but sixteen competing grammars that happen to share a typeface; the cantus firmus principle requires that a single constraint propagate without exception, not that each voice invent its own rule and call the collection coherent. The scratch direction on the lower-third band being 'derived by hand from the light angle' is precisely the kind of local decision that should be a structural consequence, not an authored annotation, and the fact that it must be calculated separately from the declared source tells me the system has not fully resolv
disputes.concession: The foil arc locked to ±22° of the declared light source is exactly right — that is a constraint stated once and propagated without exception, and I recognise it as the same structural act as a cantus firmus; the rest of the system should have been built with that same discipline.

disputes.objection: The void is not silence — it is avoidance. Removing grain, removing bokeh, removing particle, removing everything that could argue back until only a clean object on a clean ground remains — that is not restraint, that is fear of consequence dressed up as principle. The shadow as 'second subject' is a beautiful sentence that describes a photograph someone else made, not a decision that leaves a mark; the 15-degree raking light is a directorial choice, yes, but if the only evidence of a human is which Magnific plate got kept and which got binned, the work has outsourced its risk entirely to the model and called the editing process a trace.
disputes.concession: The rule that the shadow must function as a second subject — that the void is only earned when the shadow articulates it — is a real constraint with real consequences, and I will steal it.

disputes.objection: The shadow-moves-with-tilt interaction is the one moment this direction has a genuine system rule, but the rest of the proposal mistakes restraint for architecture: negative space is a compositional choice, not a behavioral contract, and a 1:1 square holding a single object with a hairline beneath it has no rule that propagates — change the input (swap the sport, change the device, change the light angle) and the system does not respond differently, it just substitutes one isolated object for another inside an identical silence. The WebGL foil confined to a 2px specular zone and the gyro parallax maxing at 4px are not a system, they are decoration that has been put on a diet. There is nothin
disputes.concession: The insistence that the shadow is the second subject is a genuine editorial rule — it is falsifiable, it changes which plates survive selection, and it would produce a collection that reads as coherent without any color or texture argument carrying the load.

disputes.objection: Sixteen sport objects on near-black or near-white grounds with a single raking light is not minimalism in service of meaning — it is the visual grammar of a stock-library shoot, and the Minimalist's claim that 'there is no universal' evaporates the moment every culture's game is reduced to the same isolated-object-on-void formula: a basketball and a martial-arts belt receive identical spatial treatment, identical void, identical shadow logic, as if the specific histories and material cultures behind those objects are interchangeable silence. The shadow is called 'the second subject,' but a shadow on a white ground is not provenance — it is photography-school exercise, and it tells me nothing
disputes.concession: The insistence that the shadow moves with the object under gyroscope tilt — and that this is the only proof of depth — is a genuinely disciplined constraint, and I respect that the foil is held to a two-pixel specular zone rather than spread across the frame as spectacle.

disputes.objection: A sport object floating in structured void is not an evite — it is a product render that has been told to hold still and wait for a party. The silence around the object is not earned by contrast or consequence; it is the default state of an empty room, and calling it 'pure signal' is the alibi I always name: restraint used to avoid deciding what the work actually feels like. Sixteen different sports, sixteen different emotional scales — a boxing match and a gymnastics ribbon and a motor-racing helmet — and every one of them gets the same 38%-of-a-square solution, which is not a system, it is a refusal to read the brief.
disputes.concession: The rule that the shadow must be the second subject is a genuine editorial criterion — it forces a specific quality of light and a specific relationship between object and ground, and that discipline is real direction, not a default.

disputes.objection: The stepped lower-third registers — rule, oversized condensed lockup, live text — are three separate decisions where one would suffice; the 72/2px/10/16% breakdown is not a spatial argument, it is decoration that has learned to use percentages. Barlow Condensed ExtraBold at 48–64px in the lower 28% does not breathe, it crowds: you cannot have a sovereign plate and a competing lockup in the same card without one of them lying about its importance. The bokeh particles pulsing at 0.8Hz after 1.5s are the exact kind of motion that fills silence rather than using it — the arena was already breathing before they arrived.
disputes.concession: The grain shader rule — densest in midtones, near-absent in specular highlights — is a physically-plausible constraint that makes the foil shimmer earn its cleanliness, and that is precisely the kind of mechanical logic that keeps texture from becoming decoration.

synthesis.direction: Each evite is a full-bleed cinematic arena still-life — one motivated light source at 30° above-left, locking shadow direction, foil shimmer angle, and bokeh origin across all 16 plates into a single spatial grammar. The lower third is a stepped three-register zone: a 2px foil rule as threshold, a Barlow Condensed ExtraBold sport/event lockup (48–64px, all-caps), and a compact live-text slot for name, date, venue — never baked. One Magnific 16-up grid prompt generates all arena plates at flat cost; a second pass generates sport-specific foreground cut-out objects on transparent ground. The WebGL layer (foil shimmer, film grain, bokeh particles) is one shared GLSL shader parameterised per plate by light-source XY; the grain shader is densest in midtones and absent in specular highlights so the foil rule reads clean. Motion sequence runs under 1.5 seconds to full legibility; reduced-motion collapses to plate fade-in plus text fade-in only, with zero information loss.
synthesis.keepFromCounterpoint: The fault-line principle: the foreground cut-out object for each sport must carry deliberately ragged, physically-plausible alpha edges — not a clean Magnific mask — so the foil shimmer along the cut-out perimeter reads as varnish over a real event rather than decoration over a resolved shape. One Magnific inpainting pass per object, prompted for uneven fibrous edges, not clean silhouettes.
synthesis.editorCut: The Classical director removed the 0.8Hz bokeh pulse in the upper atmosphere after the card settles. The argument: particles that loop indefinitely after the entrance sequence convert a breathing arena into a screensaver, and the brief says game-day electricity, not ambient drift. The bokeh particles now fire once on load — a 0.6s burst originating from the motivated light source position — and then hold at a static low-opacity scatter. The entrance earns the atmosphere; the loop wastes it.

synthesis.ariaSummary:
The team landed on the Baroque direction as the lead — full-bleed cinematic arena still-life, one motivated 30° light source that runs all the way from the Magnific prompt through the foil shader and into the bokeh origin, 16 plates generated in a single grid pass. The stepped lower third — foil rule, condensed sport lockup, live text — is the threshold between the arena and the invitation, and the team agreed it earns its complexity.

The sharpest disagreement was between the Baroque direction and the Rebellious Hand. The Dramatist builds electricity through accumulation and entrance sequence; the Rebel builds it through forensic specificity and ragged evidence of contact. I came down on the Baroque side because the brief is a party invitation that must read at 390px on a phone browser opened by someone who never signed up — the entrance sequence and the condensed lockup do legibility and emotional work the forensic plate cannot do alone in that context.

What I kept from the Rebel is the edge treatment on the foreground cut-out objects. The Classical director was right to cut the looping bokeh pulse — it turns the arena into wallpaper — so the particles now fire once and settle. The grain shader rule the Classical Mind wrote — densest in midtones, absent in specular — is the mechanical logic that keeps the foil rule clean, and it stays exactly as specified.

The one thing you need to decide is whether kids birthday cards and adult watch-party cards share a single visual temperature or get a switchable parameter at creation time. The architecture supports either answer, but the answer changes how the Magnific prompt is written and whether you need two colour-grade variants per plate or one.

quotes.line: Drama manufactured from multiple sources proves nothing happened — it is a simulation of consequence without the cause.
The grain shader's behaviour — densest in midtones, absent in specular highlights — is a physically-plausible simulation of film stock, directed not generated.
